Then for every input point $s$ and every edge $(a, b)$ of the closed polygon $v_1, \dots, v_m, v_1$ (that is, $a, b$ consecutive in this sequence), the cross product…

nodes.summary: Let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$, for an ordered field $\Bbbk$, strictly increasing in the lexicographic order on $(x, y)$. Then every vertex of their convex hull computed by the monotone chain algorithm is one of the $p_i$.
nodes.title: The hull's vertices are input points

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order. For every list of $n$ points of $\Bbbk^2$, computing their convex hull by the monotone chain algorithm costs at most $4n$, where each orientation test costs one unit.
nodes.title: The monotone chain hull makes at most $4n$ orientation tests

Let $P$ be a list of points of $\Bbbk^2$ that is strictly increasing in the lexicographic order on $(x, y)$, and suppose the points of $P$ are not all collinear: there are points $a, b, c$ of $P$ with $(b - a) \times (c - a) \ne 0$. Let $H$ be the list of points returned by the…
nodes.title: The monotone chain hull of non-collinear points turns strictly left at every vertex

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order. The convex hull of a list $P$ of points of $\Bbbk^2$ is the lower chain of $P$ followed by the upper chain of $P$ with its first and last points removed, together with its cost: the cost of computing the lower chain plus the cost of computing the upper chain.
nodes.title: Convex hull by the monotone chain algorithm

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a linearly ordered field and let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$ that are strictly increasing in lexicographic $(x, y)$ order. If $n \ge 1$, the lower chain of $p_1, \dots, p_n$ ends at $p_n$; if $n = 0$, the lower chain is empty.
nodes.title: The lower chain ends at the last point

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a linearly ordered field and let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$ that are strictly increasing in lexicographic $(x, y)$ order. If $n \ge 1$, the lower chain of $p_1, \dots, p_n$ starts at $p_1$; if $n = 0$, the lower chain is empty.
nodes.title: The lower chain starts at the first point

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a linearly ordered field and let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$ that are strictly increasing in lexicographic $(x, y)$ order, and write $\operatorname{cross}(u, v) = u_x v_y - v_x u_y$. For every $s \in \{p_1, \dots, p_n\}$ and every pair of consecutive vertices $a, b$ of the lower chain of $p_1, \dots, p_n$ we have $\operatorname{cross}(b - a, s - a) \ge 0$: the point $s$ lies on or to the…
nodes.title: Every input point lies on or left of each lower-chain edge

Write $\operatorname{cross}(u, v) = u_x v_y - v_x u_y$. Then every $c_j$ is a point of $P$; if $P$ is nonempty then…
nodes.title: Correctness of the lower chain for unsorted input

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order. For a list $P$ of points of $\Bbbk^2$, sort $P$ by merge sort into nondecreasing lexicographic $(x, y)$ order and return the lower chain of the sorted list. Only the orientation tests of the lower chain are counted; sorting costs nothing.
nodes.title: Lower chain of unsorted points

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a linearly ordered field and let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$ that are strictly increasing in lexicographic $(x, y)$ order. Then the lower chain of $p_1, \dots, p_n$ is a sublist of $p_1, \dots, p_n$: it is $p_{i_1}, \dots, p_{i_m}$ for some indices $i_1 < \dots < i_m$.
nodes.title: The lower chain is a sublist of the input

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order. For every list of $n$ points of $\Bbbk^2$, computing its lower chain makes at most $2n$ orientation tests (cross-product evaluations).
nodes.title: The lower-chain scan makes linearly many tests

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a linearly ordered field and let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$ that are strictly increasing in lexicographic $(x, y)$ order, with lower chain $c_0, \dots, c_{m-1}$. Writing $\operatorname{cross}(u, v) = u_x v_y - v_x u_y$, for every $i$ with $i + 2 < m$ we have $\operatorname{cross}(c_{i+1} - c_i, c_{i+2} - c_i) > 0$.
nodes.title: The lower chain turns strictly left

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order. The lower chain of a list of points $p_1, \dots, p_n$ of $\Bbbk^2$ is computed by Andrew's monotone chain scan: start with an empty stack and process $p_1, \dots, p_n$ in order; for each point $p = p_i$, remove the top $a$ of the stack as long as the stack has a second element $b$ with $(a_x - b_x)(p_y - b_y) - (p_x - b_x)(a_y - b_y) \le 0$, then push $p$. The lower chain…
nodes.title: Lower chain

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a linearly ordered field, let $p \in \Bbbk^2$, and write $u \times v = u_1 v_2 - v_1 u_2$ for the cross product. Given a stack of points of $\Bbbk^2$ listed top first, while the stack has at least two points, with top $a$ and next point $b$, and $(a - b) \times (p - b) \le 0$ (so $b \to a \to p$ is not a strict left turn), remove $a$. The result is the first stack reached that has fewer than two…
nodes.title: Pop step of the monotone-chain scan

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order and write $(u_1, u_2) \times (v_1, v_2) = u_1 v_2 - v_1 u_2$ for the cross product on $\Bbbk^2$. A list $q_1, \dots, q_k$ of points of $\Bbbk^2$ turns strictly left when every three consecutive points do: $(q_{i+1} - q_i) \times (q_{i+2} - q_i) > 0$ for every $i$ with $1 \le i \le k - 2$. In particular, every list of fewer than three points turns strictly left.
nodes.title: Lists of points turning strictly left

nodes.summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be a field with a linear order. For every list $p_1, \dots, p_n$ of points of $\Bbbk^2$, the upper chain of the list is the image under $p \mapsto -p$ of the lower chain of $-p_n, \dots, -p_1$, and the two computations have the same cost.
nodes.title: The upper chain is a reflected lower chain

nodes.summary: Let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$, for an ordered field $\Bbbk$, strictly increasing in the lexicographic order on $(x, y)$. If $n = 0$ the upper chain is empty; otherwise its last vertex is $p_1$.
nodes.title: The upper chain ends at the first point

nodes.summary: Let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$, for an ordered field $\Bbbk$, strictly increasing in the lexicographic order on $(x, y)$. If $n = 0$ the upper chain is empty; otherwise its first vertex is $p_n$.
nodes.title: The upper chain starts at the last point

nodes.summary: Let $p_1, \dots, p_n$ be points of $\Bbbk^2$, for an ordered field $\Bbbk$, strictly increasing in the lexicographic order on $(x, y)$. Then for every input point $s$ and every two consecutive vertices $a, b$ of the upper chain, the cross product $(b - a) \times (s - a)$ is nonnegative: $s$ lies on or to the left of the edge from $a$ to $b$.
nodes.title: Every input point lies left of the upper chain

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be an ordered field and let $p_1, \dots, p_n \in K^2$ be strictly increasing in the lexicographic $(x, y)$ order. Then the upper chain of $p_1, \dots, p_n$ is a sublist of the reversed list $p_n, \dots, p_1$: it is obtained from $p_n, \dots, p_1$ by deleting some of the entries.
nodes.title: The upper chain is a subsequence of the reversed input

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order and let $p_1, \dots, p_n \in K^2$ be any $n$ points, sorted or not. Computing the upper chain of $p_1, \dots, p_n$ costs at most $2n$, where the cost counts one unit per orientation test (one cross-product comparison) and nothing else.
nodes.title: Running time of the upper chain scan

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be an ordered field, let $p_1, \dots, p_n \in K^2$ be strictly increasing in the lexicographic $(x, y)$ order, and let $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_{m-1}$ be the upper chain of $p_1, \dots, p_n$. Then for every $i$ with $i + 2 < m$, we have $(c_{i+1} - c_i) \times (c_{i+2} - c_i) > 0$, where $(u_1, u_2) \times (v_1, v_2) = u_1 v_2 - v_1 u_2$ is the cross product: the vertices $c_i$, $c_{i+1}$, $c_{i+2}$ make a…
nodes.title: The upper chain turns strictly left

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field with a linear order. The upper chain of a list of points $p_1, \dots, p_n \in K^2$ is the lower chain of the reversed list $p_n, \dots, p_1$, together with its cost: the same scan, counting the same orientation tests. For points sorted by $(x, y)$ it runs from the last point back to the first.
nodes.title: Upper chain

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
